sections.title: From "free" to "allowed"
sections.content: You already know szabad as "free" from szabadidő ("free time") and szabadság ("vacation"). Put it in front of an infinitive and it takes on a third job: saying what's allowed by a rule — a law, a house rule, a sign on the wall. Like lehet, szabad never conjugates and takes no subject; it just states whether the rule permits something.

items.spanish: A szabályok szerint itt szabad kutyát sétáltatni.
items.english: According to the rules, walking a dog is allowed here.
Am I allowed to photograph this sign?

sections.content: lehet and szabad often overlap, but szabad is the word to reach for when a specific rule, sign, or authority is behind the answer — a szabályok szerint ("according to the rules") sentence almost always wants szabad, not lehet.
